art_style: Polished Korean fantasy webtoon for readers age8+, Mediterranean palette, clean anatomy, no text in scene images.
source_vs_adaptation: Source facts follow supplied retelling. Ages, facial features, garment colors, architecture and Siren bird form are production choices for consistency, not historical claims.

models.name: Odysseus
source_facts: A king, husband and father; clever and brave but makes mistakes.
Fights in a ten-year war, loses crew and ship, spends seven years with Calypso, returns disguised.
models.adaptation_lock: Olive-tan athletic man, dark brown eyes, short curly dark hair, full beard, left eyebrow notch. Sea-teal knee-length chiton, leather belt and sandals; cream cloak before wreck; faded tunic with no cloak in water; later gray temples and weathered beard; ragged brown cloak on return.

models.name: Penelope
source_facts: Odysseus’s wife; tests the bow and the secret of their bed before recognizing him.
models.adaptation_lock: Olive skin, brown eyes, dark crown-braided hair, plum-purple long chiton, cream shawl, simple gold earrings; adult mature face.

models.name: Odysseus’s son
source_facts: Helps his father regain their home; joins the reunion.
models.adaptation_lock: Young adult at reunion, olive skin, wavy short dark hair, clean-shaven; rust-red knee-length chiton and brown belt. Not a small child at return.

models.name: Odysseus’s men
source_facts: Travel with him; open wind bag; become pigs and are restored; use earwax and row; perish after cattle incident.
models.adaptation_lock: Adult Mediterranean men, simple ochre/navy short tunics and sandals; repeat same two recognizable secondary faces where possible. No modern military clothing.

models.name: Polyphemus
source_facts: Giant with one eye, cave and sheep; traps men; later asks his sea-god father to stop Odysseus.
models.adaptation_lock: Enormous stocky bronze-tan cyclops, exactly one eye, curly black hair and beard, rough ochre wool tunic. Eye injury remains offscreen.

models.name: Aeolus
source_facts: Keeper of winds who gives a bag containing bad winds and warns not to open it.
models.adaptation_lock: Older gray long-bearded man, sky-blue robe, deep blue cloak, brown tied leather bag.

models.name: Circe
source_facts: Magical woman turns men into pigs and later restores them; tells Odysseus to seek Tiresias.
models.adaptation_lock: Adult olive-skinned woman, amber eyes, shoulder-length dark auburn waves, forest-green robe, wine-red sash, gold bracelets, golden cup.

models.name: Hermes
source_facts: God who gives a protective magic plant.
models.adaptation_lock: Youthful adult, golden-brown curls, ivory short tunic, winged sandals, white flower with dark roots; sheet also includes a winged cap as fixed visual choice.

models.name: Tiresias
source_facts: Wise spirit warns not to hurt sun god’s cows.
models.adaptation_lock: Kind elderly translucent silver-haired man, long silver beard, pale gray robe and staff.

models.name: Odysseus’s mother
source_facts: A smiling spirit whom Odysseus cannot embrace.
models.adaptation_lock: Kind elderly translucent woman, gray low bun, pale blue robe, family resemblance to Odysseus.

models.name: The Sirens
source_facts: Sing beautifully and lure sailors toward unsafe rocks.
models.adaptation_lock: Three fully feather-covered adult bird-women, ivory/lavender plumage, wings and bird feet. Bird form is an adaptation choice, not specified in supplied retelling.

models.name: Scylla
source_facts: Sea monster with six heads, takes six men.
models.adaptation_lock: Exactly six separately countable teal-gray serpentine heads on six necks, one shared creature body; loss portrayed without visible victims.

models.name: Charybdis
source_facts: Creates a great hole in the sea able to pull a whole ship down.
models.adaptation_lock: A single huge clockwise sea whirlpool opposite Scylla’s cliff; no extra invented face.

models.name: The sun god’s cows
source_facts: Sacred cows eaten by hungry crew despite warning.
models.adaptation_lock: Healthy golden-brown cattle in green meadow; killing and wounds not illustrated.

models.name: Calypso
source_facts: Cares for Odysseus, offers eternal life, keeps him seven years, eventually helps him build a boat.
models.adaptation_lock: Adult warm olive skin, very long honey-brown waves, green-brown eyes, turquoise long robe, ivory sash and small white flowers.

models.name: Men in Odysseus’s house
source_facts: Want to marry Penelope, fail to draw bow, defeated with help of Odysseus’s son.
models.adaptation_lock: Arrogant adult men in muted cream/ochre/gray tunics, no modern clothes; no graphic combat.

models.name: Sea god, sun god and other gods
source_facts: Sea god is Polyphemus’s father; sun god becomes angry; gods eventually order Calypso to release Odysseus.
models.adaptation_lock: Keep offscreen unless directly required; convey sea danger, lightning and permission through described events, no invented deity subplot.

state_timeline.state: Same hero face, sea-teal chiton and cream cloak, intact Greek ship.
Ship destroyed; only Odysseus remains, wet tunic, cream cloak lost.
Calypso cares for hero; seven years later older weathered face, new small boat.
Ragged disguise at first, recognizably same older face; adult son; rooted tree bed remains in palace.
